    AI Overview
    The Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) is an annual, multi-day gathering of conservative activists, politicians, and media figures hosted by the American Conservative Union. It serves as a major networking and rallying event for the Republican base, often featuring speeches from prominent conservative leaders, presidential hopefuls, and influencers. 
    Key 2026 Details & Takeaways 
    • Location: The March 2026 event was held in Grapevine, Texas.
    • Theme/Tone: The 2026 conference experienced lower attendance and a "waning" energy, with discussions focusing on the "post-Trump era," foreign policy in Iran, and cultural issues.
    • Key Discussions: Attendees and speakers highlighted "America First" themes, rifts over Iran policy, and intense debate over the direction of the conservative movement, including criticism of some right-wingers deemed too moderate ("woke right").
    • Speakers: Included Texas officials like Gov. Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton, along with various content creators and activists. 
    Purpose and History 
    • Purpose: To connect conservative voters, organize activist efforts, and set the agenda for the upcoming political season.
    • Origin: Founded in 1974, with the first keynote speech delivered by Ronald Reagan. 
    Note: There are other entities known as CPAC, such as the Connecticut Parent Advocacy Center and the County Parole and Alternative Custody Unit.
